note: On this day in science. Every event below was verified against its linked source (NASA/ESA/Nobel/Britannica/APS/Nature/arXiv/...) on 2026-11-01. Covers 30 dates from 2026-11-01. If a date ever has no verified entry, ship {"date": "MM-DD"} only - the app hides the widget for that day rather than inventing history.

entries.event: The Arecibo Observatory was inaugurated in Puerto Rico - the world's largest single-dish radio telescope for the next 53 years.
The Expedition 1 crew entered the International Space Station - humanity has lived aboard continuously ever since.
The USSR launched Sputnik 2, carrying Laika - the first animal to orbit the Earth.
The first issue of the scientific journal Nature was published in London.
ISRO launched the Mars Orbiter Mission (Mangalyaan), India's first interplanetary probe.
The supernova SN 1572 ('Tycho's Nova') was first observed in Europe - a 'new star' appearing in Cassiopeia.
NASA launched Mars Global Surveyor, which went on to map the Red Planet in unprecedented detail.
Wilhelm Roentgen discovered X-rays - a discovery that transformed physics and medicine.
Apollo 4 lifted off - the first flight of the Saturn V, the rocket that would carry astronauts to the Moon.
The Soviet Union launched Zond 6 on a circumlunar flight - an uncrewed rehearsal for a crewed Moon flyby.
Tycho Brahe first observed the 'new star' (SN 1572) whose distance shattered the ancient idea of an unchanging heavens.
ESA's Philae lander touched down on comet 67P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko - the first soft landing on a comet nucleus.
Mariner 9 entered orbit around Mars - the first spacecraft to orbit another planet.
Apollo 12 launched from Kennedy Space Center toward the second crewed Moon landing.
The Soviet Buran space shuttle flew its only orbital mission - launched, flown and landed without a crew.
The Arecibo message - humanity's first interstellar radio broadcast - was beamed toward globular cluster M13.
Luna 17 deployed Lunokhod 1 - the first remote-controlled rover to roll on the Moon.
NASA launched COBE, the satellite that mapped the cosmic microwave background - the afterglow of the Big Bang.
Apollo 12's lunar module Intrepid landed on the Ocean of Storms - the second crewed lunar landing.
Zarya, the first module of the International Space Station, launched from Baikonur atop a Proton rocket.
Pilatre de Rozier and the marquis d'Arlandes made the first free flight in a hot-air balloon, over Paris.
Physicist Louis Neel was born in Lyon - his work on antiferro- and ferrimagnetism won the 1970 Nobel Prize in Physics.
Physicist Johannes Diderik van der Waals was born in Leiden - later of the real-gas equation of state.
Charles Darwin published On the Origin of Species.
Albert Einstein presented the field equations of gravitation to the physics-mathematics section of the Prussian Academy of Sciences.
France launched Asterix, its first satellite, atop a Diamant rocket - becoming the third spacefaring nation.
The Soviet Mars 2 lander became the first human-made object to reach the surface of Mars (a hard landing).
Jocelyn Bell first recorded the pulsed radio signal of PSR B1919+21 - the discovery of pulsars.
Enos the chimpanzee orbited the Earth aboard Mercury-Atlas 5 - the final step before John Glenn's orbital flight.
The Sylacauga meteorite crashed through a roof in Alabama and struck Ann Hodges - the only verified case of a meteorite injuring a person.
